candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And it came to pass after this that his name during his lifetime was raised aloft to that Son of Man and to the Lord of Spirits from amongst those who dwell on the earth' — Enoch's name lifted to the Son of Man, anticipating the climactic 71:14 'Thou art the Son of Man'. Tewahedo theological tradition reads this verse as the textual basis for the unique status accorded Enoch in the Tewahedo Synaxarium: lifted-in-name means lifted-in-priestly-status, with Enoch's intercessory role preserved as part of the heavenly liturgy.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And he set me between the two winds, between the North and the West, where the angels took the cords to measure for me the place for the elect and righteous' — measuring the place of the righteous. Tewahedo monastic geography (the actual layout of monastic complexes with directional orientation) preserves the four-cardinal-points structuring of sacred space, drawing on 70:3 and parallel Enochic texts as scriptural-cosmological anchor.
